big_idea: We line up to compare LENGTH. We cover to compare AREA.
learning_intention: We are learning to compare and order by length and area.
student_learning_goal: I can compare and order objects by length and area.
success_criteria: I can line up to find longer/shorter.
I can cover to find bigger/smaller area.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Roo and Cal — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Roo: I have 4 ribbons. Line them up — which is LONGEST? Now look at 4 cards — which has the BIGGEST AREA?
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Roo and Cal puppets. 'Friends — yesterday we named attributes. Today we COMPARE LENGTH and AREA.'

Review vocabulary. 'Length = how long. Area = how much flat space.'

Demo length. Hold up 4 ribbons of varied length. 'Line them up at one end. Now look at the OTHER end. Longest goes farthest.' Order: shortest to longest.

Demo area. Hold up 4 cards of varied size. 'Cover each card with TILES. The one needing MORE tiles has BIGGER AREA.' Place tiles on each. Count. Order: smallest to largest.

More examples:
- 4 pencils → order by length
- 4 books → order by area (cover each with tiles)
- 4 leaves → order by area

'Roo says — line up for length. COVER for area.'

'Today we ORDER 4+ objects two ways.'
student_actions: Practice lining up at one end

steps.instruction: Whole group: order 4 ribbons by length, 4 cards by area.
Three stations. Station A: Strip Order — order 5 strips by length. Station B: Tile Cover — cover 4 shapes with tiles, count. Station C: Mixed — order 4 objects by EITHER length OR area.
Stretch challenge at Station C: order 6 objects.
Discuss the line-up and cover rules. 'Length = line up. Area = cover.'
Circulate to record formative evidence on the tracker.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Mark the tracker.

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Just length ordering.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide a sentence frame: 'The ___ is longer than the ___.'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Children stand in line ordered by height (length comparison).

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: lines up at one end; counts tile coverage; orders 4+ objects.

consolidation.exit_routine: Each child writes ONE comparison: 'My ___ is longer than my ___.'

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 2 captures E2.2 mastery for length and area.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child counts tiles WITH GAPS — repairing the gap-cover trap at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
The most common Grade-1 trap on E2.2 area is the gap-cover trap: the child places tiles loosely on a shape, with gaps between them, then counts and reports an undercount. They miss that AREA requires NO GAPS and NO OVERLAPS.

This matters because area measurement depends on full coverage.

The walkthrough covers when a child leaves gaps.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station B. Child covers a card with tiles, but tiles are spaced loosely. Reports '5 tiles' when actual coverage needs 8.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You said 5. But Roo asks — push tiles together with NO GAPS.'

Guide. 'Tiles must TOUCH. No spaces. No overlaps.' Push tiles together. 'Now count again.'

Generalise. 'Roo says — area covers ALL the space. Gaps mean undercounting.'

Now practice. 'Recount with no gaps.'

If still gappy: provide a grid template under the card. Force tile alignment.

Long-term recovery: every area count uses 'no gaps, no overlaps'.
common_misconceptions: Gaps don't matter. (Repair: each gap loses tiles.)
Tile size doesn't matter. (Repair: same-size tiles only.)
Approximate counting is fine. (Repair: count every tile precisely.)

parts_outline.task: Order 4 strips from shortest (1) to longest (4).
Count tile coverage on 3 shapes. Write the area in tiles.
Find and order 3 things by length OR area.
